perso.gloss: Tailoring the message to the individual, not the segment.

agentic.gloss: Systems that don't just generate, they decide and act toward a goal.

decis.gloss: An agent choosing what to say, when, how often and on which channel — per person.

bandit.name: Bandits / RL
bandit.gloss: The maths that lets a system learn which choice wins by trying and measuring.

cep.name: CEP
cep.gloss: Customer Engagement Platform — where this messaging actually runs.

geo.name: GEO

govern.name: Governance

stories.head: OtterlyAI launches Agent Analytics to make AI crawler traffic and search ROI measurable
stories.plain: OtterlyAI now reads server logs to show marketers every AI agent and crawler visiting their site, then links that crawl activity to visibility inside AI-generated answers. This is an early but concrete step toward measuring ROI from AI search — a gap that has frustrated teams investing in GEO with no way to prove results.

stories.head: Somantra launches Brand Engagement Score to measure how deeply AI search engines discuss a brand
stories.plain: Somantra introduces a metric that scores not just whether ChatGPT, Claude, or Google AI Overviews mention a brand, but how substantively they elaborate on its differentiators across a multi-turn buyer conversation — benchmarked against competitors in the same answer. It gives marketers a new standard for measuring GEO quality, not just presence.

stories.head: InMobi Advertising launches conversational AI agent for media buyers inside its self-serve Buyer Hub
stories.plain: InMobi's new conversational agent lets agency media buyers discover premium ad inventory and negotiate deals via natural language inside a self-serve platform. It signals that agentic interfaces are replacing traditional programmatic dashboards, changing how ad buying workflows are built and who needs to operate them.

stories.head: The data trust crisis: customer data is decaying and breaking personalization ROI
stories.plain: MarTech warns that data decay is silently undermining personalization and measurement, making AI-driven decisions less reliable over time. The piece frames this as a structural governance problem, not a tooling one — relevant to any team using a CDP or running 1:1 campaigns that depend on clean, current customer data.

stories.head: Iyuno details CLOE, a multi-agent AI architecture built to maintain consistency across long-form content at scale
stories.plain: Iyuno explains how CLOE uses multiple coordinated AI agents to preserve continuity across scenes, episodes, and languages — solving a known failure mode where generative AI loses coherence in long-form content. The architecture detail matters for teams evaluating agentic content pipelines and the governance controls needed to manage them.

stories.head: OpenAI adds product carousels and AppsFlyer attribution to compete for ad dollars
stories.plain: ChatGPT now shows shoppable product carousels and ties clicks to AppsFlyer attribution — moving it from an experimental ad surface to a measurable performance channel. This changes how marketing budgets get allocated and how brands must think about visibility inside AI answers, not just search engines.

stories.head: Liferay report: Only 24% of companies have a company-wide AI usage policy as agentic adoption accelerates
stories.plain: A 2026 study finds most companies are deploying AI agents faster than they are writing rules to govern them — only 24% have a company-wide AI policy and just 25% consistently measure AI's impact with KPIs. That gap is where regulatory and brand risk accumulates, making this a priority governance story for any marketing leader.

stories.head: The AI debt hidden in faster marketing: every new capability creates governance, integration and maintenance work
stories.plain: Moving fast with AI creates a growing backlog of ungoverned prompts, unmeasured outputs, and unintegrated tools — what the author calls AI debt. The piece gives marketing ops leaders a practical frame for auditing hidden costs before they compound, which directly affects how AI tools get bought and maintained.

stories.head: Competitive intelligence tools are the first martech category being replaced by general-purpose AI
stories.plain: ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini are displacing dedicated CI platforms for battlecard creation and competitor research. The article argues stale, unverified battlecards may be a bigger risk than the tool switch itself — a concrete signal of how the martech stack is being restructured by general-purpose AI models.

stories.head: Somantra launches Brand Engagement Score to measure how substantively AI search engines elaborate on a brand
stories.plain: Somantra introduces a metric that scores how deeply ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Claude, and Perplexity discuss a brand's differentiators across multi-turn conversations — and benchmarks that against competitors named in the same answer. It gives marketers a measurable KPI for GEO, moving AI search visibility from guesswork to trackable performance.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: AI Agents Are Replacing Whole Tool Categories
body: The question has shifted from 'how does AI assist a tool?' to 'which tools does AI make redundant?' MarTech's report on the first replaced martech category signals that consolidation is no longer hypothetical — entire software segments are being absorbed into agent workflows. Launches like Peerfold's agent-first LMS and InMobi's conversational media-buying agent show the pattern repeating across CRM, email, and ad ops.

For decision-makers, this means the evaluation criteria for any new vendor purchase must now include 'could an agent handle this within 18 months?' Buying a point solution without asking that question is a planning error, not just a missed opportunity. The stack is being re-layered from the bottom up, not incrementally upgraded.

themes.head: AI Search Is Rewriting Discoverability Rules
body: ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Claude, and Perplexity are now primary surfaces where consumers first encounter products and brands — yet most marketing analytics still measure clicks to a website. Somantra's Brand Engagement Score and OtterlyAI's Agent Analytics both launched this month specifically to fill that measurement void, signalling that the tooling is finally catching up to the behaviour shift.

This creates a new optimisation discipline — Answer Engine Optimisation (AEO) and Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO) — sitting alongside, and increasingly above, traditional SEO. Brands that don't understand how AI models represent them will be invisible in the conversations that drive purchase intent, even if their search rankings look healthy.
ev: MarTech Series · Somantra Brand Engagement Score

themes.head: The Data Trust Crisis Is Quietly Poisoning Decisions
body: AI amplifies the output of whatever data you feed it — which makes degraded, stale, or siloed customer data a strategic liability rather than a housekeeping problem. MarTech's data trust crisis piece argues that AI-accelerated pipelines are outpacing the governance needed to validate inputs, meaning bad signals produce confident-sounding but wrong outputs at scale.

The 'AI debt' framing from a companion piece tightens the argument: every shortcut taken to ship faster accumulates a hidden cost in model drift, hallucinated personalisation, and eroded customer trust. The verification-can't-be-delegated piece reinforces that human sign-off on AI outputs is not optional — it is the new quality-control layer.
ev: MarTech · AI debt in faster marketing
Agile Brand · Verification can't be delegated

themes.head: Human Judgment Is Becoming a Scarcer, Pricier Skill
body: Counterintuitively, the more AI automates execution, the more valuable distinctly human skills become. Critical thinking, creative direction, ethical judgment, and strategic framing are the competencies MarTech identifies as appreciating in value — precisely because AI cannot reliably supply them. The Agile Brand piece on human judgment in AI-powered creative underlines that 'efficiency mandate' thinking undersells what senior marketers actually contribute.

This has direct workforce and budgeting implications: teams that upskill toward these meta-skills will outperform teams that simply hand off tasks to AI. The CMO planning challenge piece frames 2027 strategy as primarily a human-capability question, not a technology-spend question — the budget line for AI tools is almost secondary to who is stewarding them.
ev: MarTech · Skills AI makes more valuable
Agile Brand · Human judgment in AI creative

themes.head: Governance & Measurement Are the New Competitive Moat
body: As AI agent adoption accelerates, the organisations pulling ahead are those that have built prompt governance frameworks, cost controls, and outcome measurement before they scaled — not after. Liferay's governance report and MarTech's prompt-governance guide both argue that ungoverned AI deployment creates compliance risk and uncontrollable cost curves that negate the efficiency gains.

OpenAI's move into advertising technology and the launch of compliance-intelligence platforms like TransFi's JARVIS signal that governance is becoming a product category in its own right, not just an internal policy. Teams that treat measurement and oversight as an afterthought will face the double penalty of inflated spend and eroded trust — while competitors who got ahead of it turn governance into a differentiator.
ev: Agile Brand · Liferay on AI governance
MarTech · OpenAI competing for ad dollars

month.takeaway: Across every layer of the stack this month, the common pressure is the same: AI is moving faster than the measurement, governance, and human-judgment infrastructure needed to make it safe to trust at scale.
